text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam and Japan agreed to step up bilateral cooperation in all fields during a weekend visit by Prime Minister Hashimoto.
-- The authorities in Ho Chi Minh City are considering a ban on the employment of migrant workers from other provinces.
-- Government ministers claimed success in meeting socio-economic targets for 1996 during a meeting which ended on Saturday.
-- Vietnam's campaign against social evils has achieved encouraging results, including the discovery of an illegal video distribution ring operating between Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi.
-- Ho Chi Minh city reported 14.9 percent growth in Gross Domestic Product in 1996, slightly below a government target for the year of 15 percent.
-- The Ministry of Culture and Information has issued directives tightening controls over the advertising of tobacco and alcohol.
-- Vietnam Airlines will increase the number of domestic and foreign flights around the traditional Tet Lunar New Year holiday in early February.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has asked the Ministry of Science, Technology and Environment to ensure tight controls over the quality of consumer goods, and pollution.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's industrial growth reached 17.1 percent in 1996.
